sanskrit: evam uktas tadā sūdaḥ so 'nāsādyāmiṣaṃ kva cit nivedayām āsa tadā tasmai rājñe vyathānvitaḥ
english: Thus instructed, the cook, unable to find any meat anywhere, reported this to the king in distress.

sanskrit: rājā tu rakṣasāviṣṭaḥ sūdam āha gatavyathaḥ apy enaṃ naramāṃsena bhojayeti punaḥ punaḥ
english: But the king, possessed by the demon, addressed the cook without any anxiety, saying again and again: 'Feed him with human flesh.'

sanskrit: tathety uktvā tataḥ sūdaḥ saṃsthānaṃ vadhyaghātinām gatvā jahāra tvarito naramāṃsam apetabhīḥ
english: Saying 'So be it,' the cook then went swiftly to the place where the executioners lived, took human flesh without fear.

sanskrit: sa tat saṃskṛtya vidhivad annopahitam āśu vai tasmai prādād brāhmaṇāya kṣudhitāya tapasvine
english: He prepared it properly, mixed it with other food, and quickly served it to that hungry brahmin ascetic.

sanskrit: sa siddhacakṣuṣā dṛṣṭvā tadannaṃ dvijasattamaḥ abhojyam idam ity āha krodhaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ
english: That best of twice-born sages, seeing the food with his spiritually perfected sight, said 'This is unfit to eat,' his eyes clouded with rage.

sanskrit: yasmād abhojyam annaṃ me dadāti sa narādhipaḥ tasmāt tasyaiva mūḍhasya bhaviṣyaty atra lolupā
english: "Since that lord of men gives me food unfit to eat, therefore the craving for this very thing shall afflict that fool himself."

sanskrit: sakto mānuṣamāṃseṣu yathoktaḥ śaktinā purā udvejanīyo bhūtānāṃ cariṣyati mahīm imām
english: "Addicted to human flesh, as Shakti previously declared, he shall roam this earth as a terror to all living beings."

sanskrit: dvir anuvyāhṛte rājñaḥ sa śāpo balavān abhūt rakṣobalasamāviṣṭo visaṃjñaś cābhavat tadā
english: When the curse was spoken twice over the king, it became powerful; possessed by the force of the demon, he became bereft of his senses.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa nṛpatiśreṣṭho rākṣasopahatendriyaḥ uvāca śaktiṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā nacirād iva bhārata
english: Then that best of kings, his senses overwhelmed by the demon, having seen Shakti before him, spoke to him thus, O Bhārata:

sanskrit: yasmād asadṛśaḥ śāpaḥ prayukto 'yaṃ tvayā mayi tasmāt tvattaḥ pravartiṣye khādituṃ mānuṣān aham
english: "Since you have inflicted upon me this undeserved curse, I shall begin with you to devour human beings."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tataḥ sadyas taṃ prāṇair viprayujya saḥ śaktinaṃ bhakṣayām āsa vyāghraḥ paśum ivepsitam
english: Having said this, he immediately deprived Shakti of his life and devoured him, as a tiger devours a desired prey.

sanskrit: śaktinaṃ tu hataṃ dṛṣṭvā viśvāmitras tataḥ punaḥ vasiṣṭhasyaiva putreṣu tad rakṣaḥ saṃdideśa ha
english: Seeing Shakti slain, Viśvāmitra then directed that same demon against the remaining sons of Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: sa tāñ śatāvarān putrān vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ bhakṣayām āsa saṃkruddhaḥ siṃhaḥ kṣudramṛgān iva
english: Enraged, it devoured those hundred surviving sons of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, as a lion devours small animals.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭho ghātitāñ śrutvā viśvāmitreṇa tān sutān dhārayām āsa taṃ śokaṃ mahādrir iva medinīm
english: Vasiṣṭha, hearing that his sons had been slain by Viśvāmitra, bore that grief as a great mountain bears the earth.

sanskrit: cakre cātmavināśāya buddhiṃ sa munisattamaḥ na tv eva kuśikocchedaṃ mene matimatāṃ varaḥ
english: That best of sages resolved to destroy himself, but that foremost of the wise did not contemplate the annihilation of the Kuśika line.

sanskrit: sa merukūṭād ātmānaṃ mumoca bhagavān ṛṣiḥ śiras tasya śilāyāṃ ca tūlarāśāv ivāpatat
english: The venerable sage threw himself from the peak of Mount Meru, and his body fell upon the rocks below as if upon a heap of cotton.

sanskrit: na mamāra ca pātena sa yadā tena pāṇḍava tadāgnim iddhvā bhagavān saṃviveśa mahāvane
english: When he did not die from that fall, O Pāṇḍava, the venerable one kindled a fire and entered it in the great forest.

sanskrit: taṃ tadā susamiddho 'pi na dadāha hutāśanaḥ dīpyamāno 'py amitraghna śīto 'gnir abhavat tataḥ
english: Yet even though blazing fiercely, the fire did not burn him; O slayer of enemies, the fire became cool.

sanskrit: sa samudram abhipretya śokāviṣṭo mahāmuniḥ baddhvā kaṇṭhe śilāṃ gurvīṃ nipapāta tadambhasi
english: The great sage, overcome with grief, went to the ocean, tied a heavy rock around his neck, and plunged into its waters.

sanskrit: sa samudrormivegena sthale nyasto mahāmuniḥ jagāma sa tataḥ khinnaḥ punar evāśramaṃ prati
english: But the force of the ocean's waves cast the great sage back onto dry land; dejected, he turned back toward his hermitage.

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca tato dṛṣṭvāśramapadaṃ rahitaṃ taiḥ sutair muniḥ nirjagāma suduḥkhārtaḥ punar evāśramāt tataḥ
english: The gandharva said: Then, seeing the hermitage bereft of those sons, the sage, overwhelmed with deep grief, departed once more from the hermitage.

sanskrit: so 'paśyat saritaṃ pūrṇāṃ prāvṛṭkāle navāmbhasā vṛkṣān bahuvidhān pārtha vahantīṃ tīrajān bahūn
english: He saw a river full with fresh waters in the rainy season, carrying along many kinds of trees that grew on its banks, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: atha cintāṃ samāpede punaḥ pauravanandana ambhasy asyā nimajjeyam iti duḥkhasamanvitaḥ
english: Then a thought again came to him, O scion of the Paurava line: 'I shall submerge myself in the waters of this river,' filled with sorrow.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāśais tadātmānaṃ gāḍhaṃ baddhvā mahāmuniḥ tasyā jale mahānadyā nimamajja suduḥkhitaḥ
english: Then the great sage, binding himself tightly with cords, plunged into the waters of that great river, deeply distressed.

sanskrit: atha chittvā nadī pāśāṃs tasyāribalamardana samasthaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ kṛtvā vipāśaṃ samavāsṛjat
english: But the river cut through those cords, O crusher of enemy forces, and released the sage upright, free of bonds.

sanskrit: uttatāra tataḥ pāśair vimuktaḥ sa mahān ṛṣiḥ vipāśeti ca nāmāsyā nadyāś cakre mahān ṛṣiḥ
english: Having emerged, freed from the cords, the great sage then named that river Vipāśā — 'freed from bonds' — and so the great sage named it.

sanskrit: śoke buddhiṃ tataś cakre na caikatra vyatiṣṭhata so 'gacchat parvatāṃś caiva saritaś ca sarāṃsi ca
english: He then set his mind again upon ending his grief, and did not stay in one place; he wandered to mountains, rivers, and lakes.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa punar evarṣir nadīṃ haimavatīṃ tadā caṇḍagrāhavatīṃ dṛṣṭvā tasyāḥ srotasy avāpatat
english: Then that sage came again to a Himalayan river full of fierce crocodiles, and cast himself into its current.

sanskrit: sā tam agnisamaṃ vipram anucintya saridvarā śatadhā vidrutā yasmāc chatadrur iti viśrutā
english: That best of rivers, reflecting upon that brahmin who was equal to fire, split into a hundred streams; hence it became known as Shatadru — 'flowing in a hundred streams.'

sanskrit: tataḥ sthalagataṃ dṛṣṭvā tatrāpy ātmānam ātmanā martuṃ na śakyam ity uktvā punar evāśramaṃ yayau
english: Seeing himself deposited on dry land even there, he said to himself, 'Death is not possible for me,' and returned once more to his hermitage.

sanskrit: vadhvādṛśyantyānugata āśramābhimukho vrajan atha śuśrāva saṃgatyā vedādhyayananiḥsvanam pṛṣṭhataḥ paripūrṇārthaiḥ ṣaḍbhir aṅgair alaṃkṛtam
english: Followed by his daughter-in-law Adrishyanti, walking toward the hermitage, he suddenly heard from behind the sound of Vedic recitation, complete with its six auxiliary disciplines, full of meaning.

sanskrit: anuvrajati ko nv eṣa mām ity eva ca so 'bravīt ahaṃ tv adṛśyatī nāmnā taṃ snuṣā pratyabhāṣata śakter bhāryā mahābhāga tapoyuktā tapasvinī
english: 'Who is this that follows me?' he asked. His daughter-in-law replied: 'I am Adrishyanti by name — the wife of Shakti, O great one, a devoted ascetic.'

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca putri kasyaiṣa sāṅgasya vedasyādhyayanasvanaḥ purā sāṅgasya vedasya śakter iva mayā śrutaḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha said: 'O daughter, whose is this sound of the recitation of the Veda with its limbs? I heard it long ago from Shakti, reciting the Veda with its limbs.'

sanskrit: adṛśyanty uvāca ayaṃ kukṣau samutpannaḥ śakter garbhaḥ sutasya te samā dvādaśa tasyeha vedān abhyasato mune
english: Adrishyanti said: 'This is the embryo of Shakti, your son, arisen in my womb; for twelve years, O sage, he has been here practicing the Vedas.'

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca evam uktas tato hṛṣṭo vasiṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhabhāg ṛṣiḥ asti saṃtānam ity uktvā mṛtyoḥ pārtha nyavartata
english: The gandharva said: Thus spoken to, Vasiṣṭha, that sage of the highest fortune, rejoiced, and saying 'The lineage endures,' he turned back from death, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: tataḥ pratinivṛttaḥ sa tayā vadhvā sahānagha kalmāṣapādam āsīnaṃ dadarśa vijane vane
english: Then, having turned back, he and his daughter-in-law saw Kalmāṣapāda sitting in a deserted forest, O sinless one.

sanskrit: sa tu dṛṣṭvaiva taṃ rājā kruddha utthāya bhārata āviṣṭo rakṣasogreṇa iyeṣāttuṃ tataḥ sma tam
english: As soon as the king saw him, O Bhārata, he rose up in rage, possessed by the fierce demon, and intended to devour him.

sanskrit: adṛśyantī tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā krūrakarmāṇam agrataḥ bhayasaṃvignayā vācā vasiṣṭham idam abravīt
english: Adrishyanti, seeing that cruel-actioned one before them, spoke these words to Vasiṣṭha in a voice trembling with fear:

sanskrit: asau mṛtyur ivogreṇa daṇḍena bhagavann itaḥ pragṛhītena kāṣṭhena rākṣaso 'bhyeti bhīṣaṇaḥ
english: 'That terrible demon approaches here, O venerable one, like death itself, bearing a raised club of wood.'

sanskrit: taṃ nivārayituṃ śakto nānyo 'sti bhuvi kaś cana tvad ṛte 'dya mahābhāga sarvavedavidāṃ vara
english: 'There is no one else on earth today able to restrain him, except you, O great one, best among all who know the Vedas.'

sanskrit: trāhi māṃ bhagavan pāpād asmād dāruṇadarśanāt rakṣo attum iha hy āvāṃ nūnam etac cikīrṣati
english: 'Protect me, O venerable one, from this terrible-looking evil — the demon surely intends to devour us both here.'

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca mā bhaiḥ putri na bhetavyaṃ rakṣasas te kathaṃ cana naitad rakṣo bhayaṃ yasmāt paśyasi tvam upasthitam
english: Vasiṣṭha said: 'Fear not, O daughter — you need have no fear whatsoever of a demon. The terror you see approaching is not a demon.'

sanskrit: rājā kalmāṣapādo 'yaṃ vīryavān prathito bhuvi sa eṣo 'smin vanoddeśe nivasaty atibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: 'This is King Kalmāṣapāda, renowned on earth for his valor; it is he who dwells in this region of the forest in this terrible form.'

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ vārayām āsa tejasvī huṃkareṇaiva bhārata
english: The gandharva said: Seeing him rushing forward, the venerable and radiant sage Vasiṣṭha restrained him with a mere thunder-sound, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: mantrapūtena ca punaḥ sa tam abhyukṣya vāriṇā mokṣayām āsa vai ghorād rākṣasād rājasattamam
english: Then, sprinkling him again with water sanctified by mantras, he truly liberated that best of kings from the dreadful demon.

sanskrit: sa hi dvādaśa varṣāṇi vasiṣṭhasyaiva tejasā grasta āsīd gṛheṇeva parvakāle divākaraḥ
english: For twelve years he had been possessed — held by the power of Vasiṣṭha himself — as the sun is eclipsed at a sacred juncture.

sanskrit: rakṣasā vipramukto 'tha sa nṛpas tad vanaṃ mahat tejasā rañjayām āsa saṃdhyābhram iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Freed from the demon, the king illumined that great forest with his splendor, as the sun illumines the twilight clouds.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñām abhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ uvāca nṛpatiḥ kāle vasiṣṭham ṛṣisattamam
english: Having regained his senses, the king bowed with joined palms and spoke in proper form to Vasiṣṭha, that best of sages:

sanskrit: saudāso 'haṃ mahābhāga yājyas te dvijasattama asmin kāle yad iṣṭaṃ te brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te
english: 'I am Saudāsa, O great one, your sacrificial patron, O best of twice-born; tell me now what you desire — what shall I do for you?'

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca vṛttam etad yathākālaṃ gaccha rājyaṃ praśādhi tat brāhmaṇāṃś ca manuṣyendra māvamaṃsthāḥ kadā cana
english: Vasiṣṭha said: 'All this has come to pass as was fated. Go and rule your kingdom; and never, O lord of men, disrespect the brahmins.'

sanskrit: rājovāca nāvamaṃsyāmy ahaṃ brahman kadā cid brāhmaṇarṣabhān tvan nideśe sthitaḥ śaśvat pujayiṣyāmy ahaṃ dvijān
english: The king said: 'I shall never disrespect the best of brahmins, O brahmin; abiding by your instruction, I shall always honor the twice-born.'

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇāṃ tu yenāham anṛṇaḥ syāṃ dvijottama tat tvattaḥ prāptum icchāmi varaṃ vedavidāṃ vara
english: 'But I wish to receive from you, O best of twice-born, that boon by which I may be freed from debt to the Ikṣvāku lineage, O best among those who know the Vedas.'

sanskrit: apatyāyepsitāṃ mahyaṃ mahiṣīṃ gantum arhasi śīlarūpaguṇopetām ikṣvākukulavṛddhaye
english: 'Please go to my beloved queen, who is endowed with virtue, beauty, and fine qualities, to beget the offspring I desire, for the growth of the Ikṣvāku line.'

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca dadānīty eva taṃ tatra rājānaṃ pratyuvāca ha vasiṣṭhaḥ parameṣvāsaṃ satyasaṃdho dvijottamaḥ
english: The gandharva said: 'So I shall give it,' replied Vasiṣṭha to that king there — Vasiṣṭha, best of twice-born, firm in his pledges.

sanskrit: tataḥ pratiyayau kāle vasiṣṭhasahito 'nagha khyātaṃ puravaraṃ lokeṣv ayodhyāṃ manujeśvaraḥ
english: Then in due course the lord of men returned, accompanied by Vasiṣṭha, to Ayodhyā, that most celebrated city in the world, O sinless one.

sanskrit: taṃ prajāḥ pratimodantyaḥ sarvāḥ pratyudyayus tadā vipāpmānaṃ mahātmānaṃ divaukasa iveśvaram
english: All the people, rejoicing, came forth to welcome him — that great-souled one now free from sin — as the celestials welcome their lord.

sanskrit: acirāt sa manuṣyendro nagarīṃ puṇyakarmaṇām viveśa sahitas tena vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā
english: Without delay that lord of men, accompanied by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, entered the city renowned for its righteous deeds.

sanskrit: dadṛśus taṃ tato rājann ayodhyāvāsino janāḥ puṣyeṇa sahitaṃ kāle divākaram ivoditam
english: Then the citizens of Ayodhyā saw him, O king, like the sun risen in due season together with the Puṣya constellation.

sanskrit: sa hi tāṃ pūrayām āsa lakṣmyā lakṣmīvatāṃ varaḥ ayodhyāṃ vyoma śītāṃśuḥ śaratkāla ivoditaḥ
english: For he, the best among the prosperous, filled that Ayodhyā with splendor, as the cool-rayed moon fills the sky when it rises in the autumn season.

sanskrit: saṃsiktamṛṣṭapanthānaṃ patākocchrayabhūṣitam manaḥ prahlādayām āsā tasya tat puram uttamam
english: That excellent city, with its roads sprinkled and swept clean, adorned with raised banners, gladdened his heart.

sanskrit: tuṣṭapuṣṭajanākīrṇā sā purī kurunandana aśobhata tadā tena śakreṇevāmarāvatī
english: Filled with contented and prosperous citizens, that city shone with him at its center, O joy of the Kurus, as Amarāvatī shines with Indra.

sanskrit: tataḥ praviṣṭe rājendre tasmin rājani tāṃ purīm tasya rājño ''jñayā devī vasiṣṭham upacakrame
english: Then, after that king of kings had entered the city, the queen, by the king's command, approached Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: ṛtāv atha maharṣiḥ sa saṃbabhūva tayā saha devyā divyena vidhinā vasiṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhabhāg ṛṣiḥ
english: At the proper season, the great seer Vasiṣṭha, that sage of the highest fortune, united with the queen according to divine rite.

sanskrit: atha tasyāṃ samutpanne garbhe sa munisattamaḥ rājñābhivāditas tena jagāma punar āśramam
english: When the embryo was conceived in her, that best of sages, having been saluted by the king, departed again to his hermitage.

sanskrit: dīrghakāladhṛtaṃ garbhaṃ suṣāva na tu taṃ yadā sātha devy aśmanā kukṣiṃ nirbibheda tadā svakam
english: When the queen, having carried the embryo for a long time, did not deliver it, she then struck her own womb with a stone.

sanskrit: dvādaśe 'tha tato varṣe sa jajñe manujarṣabha aśmako nāma rājarṣiḥ potanaṃ yo nyaveśayat
english: Then in the twelfth year he was born, O bull among men — the royal sage named Aśmaka, who founded the city of Potana.

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca āśramasthā tataḥ putram adṛśyantī vyajāyata śakteḥ kulakaraṃ rājan dvitīyam iva śaktinam
english: The gandharva said: Then Adrishyanti, dwelling at the hermitage, gave birth to a son who would perpetuate Shakti's line — a second Shakti, O king.

sanskrit: jātakarmādikās tasya kriyāḥ sa munipuṃgavaḥ pautrasya bharataśreṣṭha cakāra bhagavān svayam
english: The venerable best of sages himself performed the birth-rites and other ceremonies for his grandson, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: parāsuś ca yatas tena vasiṣṭhaḥ sthāpitas tadā garbhasthena tato loke parāśara iti smṛtaḥ
english: And since Vasiṣṭha had been saved from death by him even while still in the womb, that one became known in the world as Parāśara.

sanskrit: amanyata sa dharmātmā vasiṣṭhaṃ pitaraṃ tadā janmaprabhṛti tasmiṃś ca pitarīva vyavartata
english: That virtuous soul regarded Vasiṣṭha as his father from birth, and conducted himself toward him just as toward a father.

sanskrit: sa tāta iti viprarṣiṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ pratyabhāṣata mātuḥ samakṣaṃ kaunteya adṛśyantyāḥ paraṃtapa
english: He addressed the brahmin-seer Vasiṣṭha as 'Father' in the presence of his mother Adrishyanti, O Kaunteya, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: tāteti paripūrṇārthaṃ tasya tan madhuraṃ vacaḥ adṛśyanty aśrupūrṇākṣī śṛṇvantī tam uvāca ha
english: Hearing that sweet word 'Father,' spoken with full meaning, Adrishyanti, with eyes full of tears, spoke to him:

sanskrit: mā tāta tāta tāteti na te tāto mahāmuniḥ rakṣasā bhakṣitas tāta tava tāto vanāntare
english: 'No, child — do not say "Father, Father" — this great sage is not your father. Your father, child, was devoured by a demon in the forest.'

sanskrit: manyase yaṃ tu tāteti naiṣa tātas tavānagha āryas tv eṣa pitā tasya pitus tava mahātmanaḥ
english: 'The one you think of as father — he is not your father, O sinless one. This honored one is the father of your father, that great-souled man.'

sanskrit: sa evam ukto duḥkhārtaḥ satyavāg ṛṣisattamaḥ sarvalokavināśāya matiṃ cakre mahāmanāḥ
english: Thus addressed, that great-minded, truthful best of sages was afflicted with grief, and resolved to destroy all the worlds.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā niścitātmānaṃ mahātmānaṃ mahātapāḥ vasiṣṭho vārayām āsa hetunā yena tac chṛṇu
english: Vasiṣṭha, that great ascetic, restrained the great-souled one thus resolved, by the reason you shall now hear.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca kṛtavīrya iti khyāto babhūva nṛpatiḥ kṣitau yājyo vedavidāṃ loke bhṛgūṇāṃ pārthivarṣabhaḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha said: 'There was a king on earth known as Kṛtavīrya, that bull among kings, the sacrificial patron of the Bhṛgus and of those who know the Vedas.'

sanskrit: sa tān agrabhujas tāta dhānyena ca dhanena ca somānte tarpayām āsa vipulena viśāṃ patiḥ
english: 'He, lord of the people, gratified those foremost ones, dear child, with great stores of grain and wealth at the conclusion of the Soma sacrifice.'

sanskrit: tasmin nṛpatiśārdūle svaryāte 'tha kadā cana babhūva tatkuleyānāṃ dravyakāryam upasthitam
english: 'When that tiger among kings had gone to heaven, a need for property arose at some point among his descendants.'

sanskrit: te bhṛgūṇāṃ dhanaṃ jñātvā rājānaḥ sarva eva ha yāciṣṇavo 'bhijagmus tāṃs tāta bhārgavasattamān
english: 'Learning of the wealth of the Bhṛgus, all those kings went as supplicants to those best of the Bhṛgu lineage, dear child.'
